title: Northridge Indivisible Speaker Series - REPARATIONS
description:
Join us for a powerful and timely conversation as Mandla Kayise—Commissioner at the Civil, Human Rights and Equity Department for the City of Los Angeles—speaks on reparations and presents the department’s groundbreaking report, An Examination of African-American Experiences in Los Angeles.

Mandla Kayise is the President and CEO of New World Education (NWE), a consulting organization dedicated to empowering education professionals and communities. For over two decades, he has worked across California’s education system and in local and national community development efforts, helping build pathways to success for students, professionals, and marginalized communities. Before founding NWE, he served as a director of Student Affairs and Retention at UCLA and as a project manager at the Community Coalition of South Los Angeles.

A longtime advocate for racial equity, Mandla has been recognized by organizations such as the Los Angeles NAACP Youth League, Black Women for Wellness, and the UCLA Bunche Center for African American Studies. He currently serves on several nonprofit and educational boards and is a member of the Los Angeles Reparations Advisory Commission.

Don't miss this opportunity to hear from a leader whose work continues to shape the future of equity and justice in Los Angeles.

title: Calling Swing Districts with Republican Representatives to Save Scientific Research Funding
description:
We will be calling South Asian voters living in Virginia to get out the vote for the Virginia primary election on June 17th. As the governor's race in November is likely to be highly consequential, it will be good to get voters in Virginia in the practice of getting out to vote. 

We will also be calling South Asian voters living in swing districts represented by Republicans to ask them to contact their representatives about the huge funding cuts that the Trump administration is proposing to the National Institutes of Health and the National Science Foundation. The Trump administration plans to cut 38% from the NIH and 55% from the NSF. Furthermore, they are delaying the spending of congressionally appropriated money, such that 3.8 billion dollars of scientific funding has been withheld from the NIH alone, compared with the same time last year. 

Lastly, we will be calling states represented by moderate Republican Senators to ask them to oppose the Medicaid cuts in the reconciliation bill and the Inflation Reduction Act clean energy tax credits.

title: Avelo Airline Nationwide Protest
description:
**Indivisible Mesa is joining the Coalition to Stop Avelo's nationwide call to action for a full boycott of Avelo Airlines and organizing protests at all 54 airports where they operate.** Our goal? Drive ticket sales to ZERO and make Avelo feel the consequences of profiting from deportations.

To keep the pressure on Avelo, the Coalition is planning to support additional nationwide protests and Indivisible Mesa is again joining the call!!

**Indivisible Mesa will be protesting against Avelo Airlines operating ICE deportations on Saturday, July 26th!**

The message to **City Hall** is simple: **"Stop funding Avelo with local dollars."**

The message to **travelers** is simple: **"Boycott Avelo, don't give them your money."**

The message to **allies** is simple: **"Join us. Stand for justice. Fight inhumanity."**

And the message to the **world** is powerful: 
*We stand for families. 
We stand for immigration rights. 
We stand for due process. 
We stand for all Americans who are feeling scared and vulnerable. 
We stand against companies that sacrifice people for profit. 
We stand against blood money and we stand against deals-with-the-devil. We stand against Avelo's contract with ICE. 
And we stand together, together, together. 
We will win this fight! 
We will force Avelo to cancel its ICE contract.**

Protest locally, speak nationally.

🌄 Indivisible Mesa will be at the intersection of East Ray Rd and Power Rd.

title: MI: Stop Microplastics Now! Michigan Campaign Call
description:
Every day, people across the United States and the world are ingesting microplastics — broken down pieces of plastic — in our drinking water. It’s estimated that the average person consumes the equivalent of *a credit card of plastic each week!*

Microplastics present significant health risks, yet the EPA hasn’t taken steps to monitor and regulate them. We deserve to know how microplastics are impacting our drinking water. 

**If seven governors formally petition the EPA to monitor microplastics, the EPA is obligated to respond unless they can provide a legally sound justification for their decision.**

title: Cumberland County Voter ID Workshop
description:
We invite you to a Cumberland County Voter ID Workshop on **Tuesday, June 24th, from 6:30 to 8:00 PM**. The workshop will be held in person at Legacy Rolls, 1161 N Bragg Blvd, Spring Lake.

Please join us for an interactive session designed to equip Cumberland County residents with the knowledge and tools to navigate North Carolina’s voter ID requirements—and learn how to get an accepted ID.

**What to Expect**:

- **Learn What Counts**: Find out which photo IDs are accepted for voting in North Carolina, including driver’s licenses, state IDs, passports, military/veteran IDs, tribal IDs, approved student and public employee IDs, and free county-issued voter IDs.

- **Get Hands-On Help**: Apply on-site for a free county voter ID or learn how to get a no-fee ID from the DMV.

- **Take-Home Resources**: You will receive easy-to-read guides in English and Spanish, with a list of accepted IDs and step-by-step application instructions.

We hope to see you there!

Questions? Contact Lynndora at lynndora@democracync.org

title: Sign the Petition for SB1 Referendum at Lima Public Library
description:
Come sign the petition for SB1 Referendum at the **Lima Public Library** this Saturday from 9am-12pm.

## WHAT IS SENATE BILL 1?

- Senate Bill 1  (“The Higher Education Destruction Act”) was signed into OH law by Gov. DeWine on March 28, 2025 and goes into effect on June 25, 2025. 
- SB1 guts collective bargaining rights for faculty unions, removes job protections for educators & bans striking time for full-time staff.
- SB1 allows colleges & universities to end programs & terminate faculty positions without warning or cause.
- SB1 bans most diversity, equity & inclusion programs and staff training in higher education.
- We have until June 22 to collect 250,000 signatures in OH and get a repeal measure on the Nov. ballot.
- Republicans in OH leadership have now introduced bills (SB113 & HB155) targeted at grades K-12. We must stop attacks on public education!
- For more information, visit [ohiosb1petition.com](ohiosb1petition.com)
- Sign the petition to repeal SB1!

title: Winston-Salem Screening of American Coup: Wilmington 1898
description:
We invite you to join Democracy North Carolina, The NAACP Winston-Salem Branch, Goler Memorial AME Zion Church Women’s Ministry, PBS North Carolina, and Working Films for a screening of *American Coup: Wilmington 1898* on **Friday, June 20th, from 5:30 PM to 7:30 PM**. 

**This in-person event will take place at Goler Memorial AME Zion Church (3894 Northampton Dr, Winston-Salem, NC 27105).**

The event will begin promptly at 5:30 PM with a light reception. The film screening will start at 6:00 PM, followed by a panel discussion, audience Q&A, and a closing prayer.

*American Coup: Wilmington 1898* is a documentary that tells the little-known story of a deadly race massacre and a carefully orchestrated insurrection in North Carolina’s largest city in 1898 — the only coup d’état in US history.

The film shares the story of how self-described white supremacists used intimidation and violence to destroy Black political and economic power and overthrow Wilmington’s democratically elected, multi-racial government. Black residents were murdered, and thousands were banished. The story of what happened in Wilmington was suppressed for decades until descendants and scholars began to investigate. Today, many of those descendants — Black and white — seek the truth about this intentionally buried history.

We hope you join us for this free screening and discussion to learn more about the massacre and coup, its place in US history, and its lasting impact. 

Together, we can ensure that the lessons of Wilmington’s past inform conversations around democracy today.

Questions? Contact Linda at linda@democracync.org.

title: HEALTHCARE IS A HUMAN RIGHT, NOT A LUXURY ONLY FOR THE RICH
description:
Millions lacking health insurance. Millions more who can’t afford medical care even with insurance.  Over 500,000 bankruptcies yearly due to medical debt. Costs rising and hospitals closing.  Health care in the U.S. is a disaster!  What can be done? 

Join Progressive Democrats of America – Kansas chapter’s inaugural meeting when Dr. Mark Krasnoff, full-time practicing internist at SSM Health in St. Louis and board member of Physicians for a National Health Program-Missouri, will provide an in-depth look at how universal single payer healthcare could fix our broken system.  We’ll talk about the challenges we face in changing the system, the current Medicare for All bill in Congress, and how we can get active in Kansas to help make this change happen. 

Whether you’re a long-time universal healthcare advocate or brand new to the subject, come learn and organize with us so we can have a future where healthcare is a human right.
